title: People connect fly brains to games and bodies.
notes:
These related projects use different datasets, models, and input adapters. Eon connects a whole-brain model to an embodied fly simulation. NeuroCraft Fly uses a MaleCNS leaky-rate model and scripted Minecraft body programs. DOOMFLY maps visual inputs and neural readouts to a Doom controller. Its baseline uses 3,335 R1–R6 brightness inputs. Later variants add other channels. Those projects do not validate this workshop's escape behavior.

Our workshop uses the pinned Doodle Fly v783 LIF runtime. Its 138,639-neuron network offers many possible input populations. We select a small escape pathway so the retrieval mechanism stays legible.

Sources: https://eon.systems/updates/embodied-brain-emulation ; https://github.com/evnsnclr/neurocraft-fly-public ; https://github.com/nftechie/doomfly/tree/71ecf53d78eaffaf1a57ed7b0ccf5d458abc9f33 ; https://github.com/dtecx/doodle-fly/tree/2a8a0311e4e488e9bf9a7f8e79e42ffb8bcaadf5 . Screenshot credits are in _maintainer/assets/NOTICE.md.

title: Retrieval supplies stored evidence for the current task.
notes:
Retrieval selects stored information relevant to the current task. The application gives a query to the search engine. The engine returns records. The application uses their content in its next decision.

Use the documentation example. A question says undo a deployment. A useful guide says restore the previous version. Matching meaning can help when wording differs. An assistant can put the returned guide into its context before composing an answer. Search, selection, and the consumer remain separate parts.

The fly follows the same contract. Its current cue is the query. Past sensory episodes are records. The neural model consumes the selected input recording. Retrieval is also useful for document search, recommendations, and finding past tool observations. These examples are illustrative.

Source: https://qdrant.tech/documentation/overview/vector-search/

title: The encoder defines what similarity can mean.
notes:
An encoder maps an input into numerical coordinates. A text embedding model can place related meanings near each other. Other encoders represent images, audio, or sensor features. Both stored inputs and new queries must use compatible encoders and vector dimensions. A search engine compares vectors supplied to it.

The fly uses an eight-dimensional engineered cue representation. Its first two values encode a simulated pulse-pattern phase. Small simulated sensor noise makes later queries differ from stored vectors. The vector uses the current visible cue. It does not contain the future sweep label or the identity of the correct episode. The cue design is a teaching device. It does not establish quality for a text embedding model.

Ask which distinctions the representation must preserve in the audience's applications. Source: _internal/escape/scene.py encode(); https://qdrant.tech/documentation/concepts/vectors/

title: Vector search ranks similar representations.
notes:
Cosine similarity compares vector direction. A score describes similarity under the chosen representation. It is not the probability that a stored claim is true. A threshold rejects sufficiently different representations. A limit sets the maximum number of results.

HNSW organizes vectors in a layered graph for approximate nearest-neighbor search. Coarse links help reach a useful area, then denser links refine the search. This diagram is schematic. It is not a trace of Qdrant visiting nodes. The workshop collection is small, and the index is forced for demonstration. Do not make performance or scale claims from this task.

Qdrant Edge uses a named cue vector with cosine distance. The live query returns actual point IDs, scores, and payloads. Source: _internal/escape/scene.py shard(); https://qdrant.tech/documentation/concepts/indexing/ ; https://qdrant.tech/documentation/edge/edge-api/reading-data/

title: Fixed neural wiring turns input into spikes.
notes:
The network contains 138,639 neurons and 15,091,983 directed connections from FlyWire v783. The anatomical image uses actual neuron anchor positions. Bright points are neurons active in the computed scene. The voltage sketch is schematic.

A leaky integrate-and-fire neuron integrates incoming current, leaks toward rest, and emits a spike after crossing a threshold. Rest and reset are -52 mV. The threshold is -45 mV. LPLC2 and LC4 populations feed the giant-fiber escape pathway. We read the two DNp01 neurons.

This is Doodle Fly's Float32 runtime with Shiu-style parameters. Independent dense integration checks total spike counts and DNp01 times, including a continuous-state replay fixture. Brian2 scheduling equivalence and biological escape timing remain unestablished. The world and body use declared engineering rules.

Sources: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07763-9 ; https://github.com/dtecx/doodle-fly/tree/2a8a0311e4e488e9bf9a7f8e79e42ffb8bcaadf5 ; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960982219301381 ; artifacts/plans/evidence/dense-runtime-validation.json.

title: A recalled episode adds earlier sensory input.
notes:
The current cue becomes a vector query. Qdrant returns the winning episode with a reference to immutable sensory input events. The adapter replays those events from cue recognition, preserving relative timing, targets, amplitude, and duration. It keeps the natural sensory stream active. The model's wiring stays fixed.

The natural looming input arrives when the fixed world makes the swatter visible. LPLC2 and LC4 inputs can then activate DNp01. The body starts an engineered escape only after the neural readout fires. A score or a stored sweep label never calls movement. A quiet episode replays quiet sensory content and produces no escape response in this task.

This is external episodic memory connected through a designed sensory adapter. The scene uses 45 ms for refuge clearance and a strike at 200 ms. Those values describe the game. Source: fly_brain.py; _internal/escape/neural/runtime.ts; _internal/escape/scene.py.

title: Store a cue vector with a usable episode.
notes:
This is actual personal point 106. Fly A observed the sweep in cycle 1, which is scene two in the display. The vector represents that earlier cue. The payload retains the source, arena, model protocol, observation cycle, observed event, and recording reference.

The input recording contains an 80 ms window of directly observed external sensory events. Its content hash identifies events, target populations, duration, and protocol. The reference is 736f49e7d40bc176a984f504bfc25b3e78b75363cdebbdaff1b2f1b4c3ce1bff. Qdrant stores the compact reference rather than duplicating thousands of event pairs in every payload. The local neural worker owns immutable recordings for this run.

The later query differs from the stored cue and retrieves this point at cosine 0.999984. Observed event metadata supports provenance and conflict checks. The selected recording's content determines the neural input. Source: artifacts/escape-runs.json personal Fly A cycle five; _internal/escape/neural/runtime.ts.

title: Write verified experience after the observation ends.
notes:
A query can use only earlier completed observations. The scene collects decisions for every fly, runs the neural and engineered world outcome, then publishes the observed episodes after the cycle. No fly can read another fly's same-cycle future.

A sweep remains a threat observation when the fly dodges it. Injury and the environmental event are separate fields. Calling a dodged sweep safe would corrupt the next decision. A quiet record becomes valid after the warning-only observation window ends. Recalled guesses never become new direct observations.

The world advances each neural session continuously for 600 ms per encounter. The stored sensory window lasts 80 ms. The display slows and shows the first 350 ms for explanation. The publication boundary follows the full observation. Source: _internal/escape/scene.py buffered writes; _internal/escape/neural/runtime.ts.

title: Two operations create personal memory.
notes:
Open memory.py. Implement remember with UpdateOperation.upsert_points. Implement recall with QueryRequest and Query.Nearest using the cue vector. Construct the eligibility filter with arena orchard and the supplied PROTOCOL. Add optional source exclusion for the next build. Set limit three, threshold 0.98, and with_payload=True.

The slide names the filter eligible for readability. The implementation can construct it inline. Keep quiet observations eligible. Complete decide by returning best.payload["recording"]. title: The same cue can produce an earlier escape.
notes:
Run Personal. Playback opens at the matched repeat ambush, scene six. Earlier computed scenes include the fly's first observed injury. Point 106 now supplies its own recorded sensory input. The ghost shows the same scene without retrieval.

For Fly A, the no-memory DNp01 onset is 179.6 ms. With the retrieved episode it is 4.5 ms. The fixed clearance rule adds 45 ms. The strike stays at 200 ms. No-memory clearance is 224.6 ms. Memory clearance is 49.5 ms. The difference comes from earlier input, with fixed wiring and natural sensory schedule.

Pause and scrub to compare the input raster, escape activity, and movement. Open Inspect query. Mute recall, then restore the full path. Retrieval still runs while the muted channel prevents replay from entering the model. The ordinary reflex remains available. Source: artifacts/escape-runs.json matched Fly A cycle five; fly_brain.py.

title: Shared evidence helps before a first encounter.
notes:
A recipient can have no personal experience of this threat and still retrieve Scout's observed episode. Scout has directly observed one orchard sweep and one quiet orchard cycle. Kitchen Scout also observed a quiet cycle, with a different cue association in a different arena. All conditions compute these source observations. Only shared memory allows the recipient to query them.

The shared shard runs inside the Python application through Qdrant Edge. It supplies another access scope. This workshop models access to other agents' evidence within one process. Network synchronization is outside the lesson. All flies use the same model protocol, so this is provenance-controlled reuse rather than a claim about transfer between different brains.

For builders, local agent memory can stay on a device, while an explicit shared source supplies team observations. Choose access rules before ranking. Sources: pipeline.py; https://qdrant.tech/documentation/edge/

title: Shared memory adds one read and one write.
notes:

title: Safe evidence keeps the fly feeding.
notes:
Run Shared. On the first threat, Fly A retrieves Scout's episode and fires DNp01 at 4.5 ms. It clears refuge at 49.5 ms before the fixed 200 ms strike. The recipient has not experienced this threat itself. Continue to a similar quiet cue.

The safe and threat cue prototypes have cosine similarity about 0.995. Both pass the 0.98 threshold. A closer quiet episode can rank first. Its replay produces neural input without DNp01 escape activity. Thresholding alone does not explain the safe behavior.

The safe-episode-removal control still survives, but produces 18 false escapes per six-fly run and keeps only 1.5% of safe feeding. The complete shared path produces zero false escapes and retains 100%. Those controls use five held-out seeds. The same waste occurs when always replaying the threat episode on every cue. Source: _internal/escape/data/evaluation.json. These values describe the engineered task.

title: Measure the decision, including its cost.
notes:
The table uses 20 declared held-out world seeds, 10000 through 10019, with six flies per run. Means: no memory has zero survivors, 12 hits, and 100% safe feeding retained. Personal memory has six survivors, six hits, and 100% safe feeding. Shared memory has six survivors, zero hits, and 100% safe feeding. Each mode sees the same scheduled world and natural input events.

The causal controls matter. Muting replay restores 12 hits. Disconnecting sensory outputs prevents DNp01 escape. Disabling the escape readout preserves spikes and prevents movement. Removing donor evidence restores the personal-memory harm level. The always-escape control survives but wastes 98.5% of safe feeding.

The representation and world are engineered. The normal reflex succeeds in clear-view trials. Sensitivity includes 20, 45, and 90 ms clearance times. At 20 ms the reflex can already avoid the task's threats, so memory has less outcome value. Similarity cannot recover an unrepresented distinction. Source: _maintainer/evaluation-protocol.json; _internal/escape/data/evaluation.json.

title: Use the same contract in an AI agent.
notes:
Map this worked example to a deployment assistant. The current tool observation replaces the fly cue. A compatible text encoder produces the query vector. Search returns a verified past incident or runbook with service, source, version, and time metadata. The agent uses that content when proposing its next action. Store the new outcome only after observing it.

The fly consumes recorded sensory events. A language model can consume retrieved text in its context. Retrieval keeps relevant external information available without changing the consumer's weights. The application still validates evidence and controls actions.

For a real workload, choose the encoder, metadata access rules, freshness policy, and downstream evaluation. Measure whether the returned evidence changes the right decision and what a false match costs. The deployment incident on this slide is illustrative, not a second implemented demo.
